prompt: You buy $3$ items costing \$$2.49$ each. How much total?
hint: Three items at the same price is a repeated addition. Which single operation gives the total for equal amounts?

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a friendlier price first: three items at $2.50$ dollars each. The real price is one cent less per item.
Three items at the same price is a repeated addition. Which single operation gives the total for equal amounts?
Multiply $2.49 \times 3$ by splitting the price: $2 \times 3$ for the dollars and $0.49 \times 3$ for the cents. Then add the two results.
$6 + 1.47 = 7.47$, so the three items cost $7.47$ dollars in total.

explanation: Three items at the same price means multiplying the price by $3$: $2.49 \times 3$.
Split the price into dollars and cents so each part is easy: $2 \times 3 = 6$ and $0.49 \times 3 = 1.47$.
The distributive property lets you add the two partial products: $6 + 1.47 = 7.47$.
The total cost of the three items is $7.47$ dollars.
